title: Disambiguate a same-spelling word
observableEvidence: Explains how context disambiguates a sound-alike or same-spelling pair.
prompt: In the sentence "At dusk, a bat flew out of the attic and swooped after moths," which meaning of bat fits? Enter one option exactly: animal or sports equipment.
solutionRepresentation: animal. The context words "flew", "swooped" and "after moths" describe something alive that flies and hunts insects, which fits the flying animal. A piece of sports equipment cannot fly out of an attic by itself or chase moths.
solutionMethod: Find the context words that only one meaning of the same-spelling word can satisfy.

deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Provisional SP-1 ruling C-1: contest mode keeps a legacy text validator whose only accepted answer is the exact option text listed in the prompt. Matching is case-insensitive and ignores trailing punctuation; any other wording is rejected.

hintSteps.prompt: The word bat has the same spelling for two different meanings. The other words in the sentence decide which one is meant.
hintSteps.question: Which words in the sentence describe what the bat does?

hintSteps.prompt: Test each meaning in the sentence. Ask whether that meaning could do the actions the sentence describes on its own.
hintSteps.question: Could each meaning fly, swoop and follow moths by itself?

hintSteps.prompt: Example with a different word: in "She wound the bandage around the cut," wound means wrapped, not an injury, because a bandage is wrapped around something.
hintSteps.question: Which meaning of bat do the action words in this sentence point to?

accessibilityNotes: All information is presented in text. Sounds are described in words, not phonetic symbols. No visual formatting, audio or official list data is required.
